Fitts's Law.definition: Time to acquire a target depends on distance and size.
checklist: Increase padding for small text links

Hick's Law.definition: Decision time increases with number/complexity of choices.

Miller's Law.definition: Average person can keep 7±2 items in working memory.
checklist: Use progressive disclosure for complex forms

Jakob's Law.definition: Users prefer familiar patterns similar to other sites.

Aesthetic–Usability Effect.definition: Attractive things feel easier to use.

Doherty Threshold.definition: System response time should be under 400ms for optimal flow.

Tesler's Law.definition: Every application has inherent complexity that cannot be removed.

Serial Position Effect.definition: Users remember first and last items in a list best.
checklist: Avoid burying key options in middle

Von Restorff Effect.definition: Items that stand out are more memorable.

Law of Proximity.definition: Spatially close items are perceived as related.

Law of Similarity.definition: Similar looking elements are perceived as related.
checklist: Use consistent styling for similar functions

Law of Continuity.definition: Elements arranged on a line or curve are perceived as related.
checklist: Align elements to create visual flow

Law of Closure.definition: Mind fills in gaps to create complete shapes.

Figure-Ground.definition: Eye separates objects from their background.

Law of Prägnanz.definition: People perceive complex images in their simplest form.
